comments.author: @Gargamel-n-Rudmilla
comments.text:
There are a lot of bottlenecks in Chip Design  where probablistic and or learning algorithms ( I do not call AI inteligent at all since they have no emotional intelligence or empathy nore awareness of oneself so are not conscious, unlike living animals and humans.
Humans are obiously animals also but have ligh level brain functions that enable us to have complex emotional and psychological states. I guess social animals like Elephants, Apes, Dolphines etc have the same high level capacity but they have not chosen/evolved to reach the hights and inevitable lows that humans have evolved into) .

Anyways chip P&R - place and routing - are the mid-end of the design process.
They are another one of the optimisation process. Placement seeks to optimise area, power and speed at a lower representions of the chip functionality. It uses the netist (connectivity of the key blocks in the design) and then places their geometry (usually some oblong) into a digital space represented by the pads on the chip. The pads are where the wires connect the silicon that the chip is made from called a die to the packaging via wires being bonded to the pads and to the pads on the package. More advanced packages called Ball Gid Arrays have massive pinout capacity and are used for Microprocessors, Memory chips, DSP, Graphics and AI.
Anyways there are many placement optimisation algorithms and so AI will just be another one of those competing in this space.
Routing is a much more complex challenge and maybe where AI is best placed to beet conventional algorithms since one not only has to be constrained by the placement, one needs to assess the impact of the wire performance so its resistance, capacitance and for very long wires that carry high currents and high bandwith signals the wires inductance. 
Then there are capacitive coupling issues between other  signals and power lines  that inject noise into the the signal line being optimised, that need to be considered and checked against timing constraints.
Each signal has to go through these optimisations. Fortumately designers are only very concerned about optimising the critical path at each of the design stages but at the place and route stage one can get stuck in an eternal loop since optiming for one critical path may result in inducing a critical path in another signal line since one has to achieve local as well as global timing constraints.
In chip design the highest perfornance chips that cost the most and are the larest and most power hungy have these deadly timimg loops. No even AI can get out of them. Designers will know they have reached the limit when they are stuck in this death loop of not being able to meet timing constraints at the routing level and only have two options. A- reduce the timing constraint by slowing down the critical path and thus the chip speed or N- doing the placement of the key blocks again but this time using the routing already done as a guidance for the new run of the placememt tool. In this way there is a back and forth between placement runs and routing runs to shoehorn the design into meeting agressive timing specs of high performance chips.
AI may also help by having a high level of predicting if placed chips will have any routing issues - commonly known as congestion .
